question: What is tuition cost for the program?
text:
Tuition and course fees displayed are for Summer 2026, Autumn 2026, Winter 2027, and Spring 2027 [4](https://datascience.uchicago.edu/education/tuition-fees-aid/). The tuition for the MS in Applied Data Science program is:

*   **12 courses:** $6,830 per course*, totaling $81,960+^ [4](https://datascience.uchicago.edu/education/tuition-fees-aid/)
*   **18 courses:** $6,830 per course*, totaling $122,940+^ [4](https://datascience.uchicago.edu/education/tuition-fees-aid/)

Additionally, there is a non-refundable Program Enrollment Deposit of $1,500, which is credited toward your first quarter’s tuition balance [4](https://datascience.uchicago.edu/education/tuition-fees-aid/).

Please note that tuition is expected to increase 3-7% per fiscal year, and those completing the program over 2 fiscal years will be subject to an increased tuition rate in the second fiscal year [2](https://datascience.uchicago.edu/education/tuition-fees-aid/). For a full list of direct and indirect expenses, please visit the Cost of Attendance page [2](https://datascience.uchicago.edu/education/tuition-fees-aid/).

question: Does the online program provide visa sponsorship?
text: No, the Online Program does not provide visa sponsorship [1](https://datascience.uchicago.edu/education/masters-programs/ms-in-applied-data-science/how-to-apply/) [2](https://datascience.uchicago.edu/education/masters-programs/ms-in-applied-data-science/international-students/) [4](https://datascience.uchicago.edu/education/masters-programs/ms-in-applied-data-science/faqs/).

sources.title: How to Apply
sources.heading: International Students
sources.text:
Only the full-time, in-person program is visa-eligible.
International students are also welcome to apply to our Master’s in Applied Data Science Online program, which does not require citizenship or permanent resident status and does not provide visa sponsorship.

sources.title: International Students
sources.heading: Applying as an International Student
sources.text:
International students are an important part of the MS in Applied Data Science community, bringing global perspectives into every classroom.
The program offers different formats:
Only the full-time, in-person program is eligible for student visa sponsorship
The online program is open to international students worldwide, but it does not provide visa sponsorship
Not sure which option is right for you? Our admissions team can help you think through your next steps.

sources.title: FAQs
sources.heading: International Students › Which Master's in Applied Data Science provides students with visas?
sources.text: The full-time, In-Person (https://datascience.uchicago.edu/education/masters-programs/in-person-program/) 1-Year 12-Course Program & 2-Year Thesis Track 18-Course Program are visa eligible.

sources.title: FAQs
sources.heading: Online Program › Do I need to be a US citizen or permanent resident to apply to Master's in Applied Data Science Online Program?
sources.text: No, students do not have to be US citizen or resident to partake in the Online Program (https://datascience.uchicago.edu/education/masters-programs/online-program/) . Please note that the Online Program (https://datascience.uchicago.edu/education/masters-programs/online-program/) is not eligible for visa sponsorship.

sources.title: International Students
sources.heading: Information for International Applicants
sources.text:
Application timing depends on your visa status.
If you require a new student visa (F-1): You must apply by the international application deadline. For the Autumn 2026 entry, that deadline has passed. Applicants who require a new visa should plan to apply for a future term.
If you are currently studying in the U.S. and transferring your SEVIS record: You may still be eligible to apply by the final application deadline.

question: What are the minimum TOEFL and IELTS scores?
text: For the Master’s in Applied Data Science program, the minimum English language proficiency scores are: TOEFL: 102 (prior requirement) or 5 (current requirement; no subscore requirement); and IELTS, 7 (no subscore requirement) [1](https://datascience.uchicago.edu/education/masters-programs/ms-in-applied-data-science/how-to-apply/) [2](https://datascience.uchicago.edu/education/masters-programs/ms-in-applied-data-science/international-students/).

sources.title: Proof of English Proficiency
sources.heading: Who Must Provide Proof of English Proficiency
sources.text: Applicants to the graduate schools and divisions of the University of Chicago, regardless of citizenship, must either meet one of our waiver criteria (below) or submit proof of English language proficiency. This policy applies to all* graduate programs; the score level required for admission varies by program. Only the TOEFL iBT or IELTS Academic tests are accepted as proof of proficiency.

University English Language Institute (https://esl.uchicago.edu/)

sources.title: Proof of English Proficiency
sources.heading: Acceptable Tests
sources.text:
In order to meet the proof of proficiency requirement, students may submit either:
Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) internet-based test (iBT), including tests taken online at-home, or in a testing center
Applicants who submit the IELTS One Skill Retake are also required to submit the original IELTS score report.
Only the Academic versions of IELTS are accepted, not the General Training Reading/Writing test.
We do not accept any other proficiency tests, exams, equivalent coursework, certificate/certifications, endorsement from faculty, and/or other measurement other than the TOEFL iBT or IELTS Academic. This includes the IELTS “Indicator” test, the TOEFL ITP Plus, Duolingo, or any other test.
